title: Anthropic Stock Falls 28% From Its High, Back Near IPO Price
summary: Anthropic stock is down 28% from its high and near its $83 IPO price. What drove the slide, the deal terms, large-IPO history and analyst forecasts.
body_markdown:
In a concurrent private placement at the same $83.00 price, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom,[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) unit Google LLC, Micron Technology, Microsoft,[Nvidia (NVDA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nvda/) and TSMC Partners bought Class N shares worth about $26.0 billion, the company said. Nvidia has invested a combined $20 billion in Anthropic, $10 billion through a partnership announced in November 2025 and $10 billion in a share purchase tied to the IPO, per Al Jazeera. Anthropic has also committed $110 billion to Amazon and at least $121.3 billion to Google for computing infrastructure under long-term agreements, the outlet reported.


The table below sums up the deal terms in Anthropic's Nov. 20 closing announcement.


Deal term Detail


Class A shares sold in the IPO, including the underwriters' option 1,127,000,000


Shares sold by Anthropic 1,103,351,354


Shares sold by selling stockholders 23,648,646


Gross IPO proceeds About $93.5 billion


Class N shares in the concurrent private placement 313,253,007


Private placement proceeds About $26.0 billion


Combined gross proceeds About $119.5 billion


Listing Nasdaq Global Select Market, symbol ANT, from Nov. 19, 2026


## Large US IPOs Fell a Median 53% in Their First Year


The Motley Fool cited First Trust and Bloomberg data on the 15 largest US[initial public offerings](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) between 2006 and 2025. The median stock fell 53% below its IPO price at some point in its first year and ended that year 32% below it, while 11 of the 15 traded below their IPO price at the end of year one. The author cautioned that historical patterns cannot predict the performance of individual stocks.


Some of the demand for the listing may reflect investors not wanting to miss a rare chance at exposure to a leading AI company, "even if its long-term profitability remains uncertain," Lukas Muehlbauer, an associate at IPOX, told Reuters, as reported by Al Jazeera.


## What Do Analysts Forecast for Anthropic Revenue?


Analysts cited by The Motley Fool expect rapid revenue growth through the end of the decade. Pierre Ferragu of New Street Research forecasts revenue of $505 billion in 2030, up from an estimated $53 billion in 2026, as computing capacity rises sixfold. David Hynes of Canaccord Genuity sees $224 billion in 2028, from an estimated $55 billion in 2026, and calls Anthropic "one of the most important enterprise technology franchises of the AI era," while Goldman Sachs expects revenue above $600 billion by 2030.


Not every analyst is upbeat. Felix Wang of Hedgeye Risk Management, who began coverage in the week of Nov. 23 according to Bloomberg, holds the most bearish view among the analysts in the report. These revenue figures are the analysts' own estimates.
